name: Denmark

legislature.name: Folketing (179)
legislature.detail: Supported by Red–Green Alliance, Alternative and Greenlandic/Faroese members.

synopsis: Frederiksen began a third term in June 2026 at the head of a four-party centre-left minority government. Greenland and rapid military build-up top the agenda after a crisis over US designs on the territory.
policies: Greenland negotiations with the US and Greenland's government

name: Greenland (Denmark)
system: Autonomous territory of the Kingdom of Denmark with parliamentary self-government
judiciary: Greenland courts within the Danish legal system.
synopsis: A broad national-unity coalition governs in response to US interest in acquiring Greenland. The long-term goal of independence is shared but its pace is debated.
policies: Resisting annexation while expanding US/Danish cooperation
challenges: Economic dependence on Danish block grant

name: Sweden

legislature.name: Riksdag (349)
legislature.control: Opposition parties (S, V, C, MP) 176 vs outgoing Tidö parties (M, SD, KD, L) 173
legislature.detail: S 99, M 70, SD 62, V 30, C 25, KD 22, MP 22, L 19. Speaker Andreas Norlén (M). On 15 Oct 2026 the Riksdag rejected Magdalena Andersson (S) as PM of a Social Democrat-only government, 248 against and 99 in favour, and on 3 Nov 2026 it rejected Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist (C), 324 against and 25 in favour. Two of the four PM votes allowed before a snap election must be called have now failed. On 24 Nov 2026 the Speaker proposed Ulf Kristersson (M) as PM of a Moderate, Centre, Christian Democrat and Liberal government; the Riksdag votes on 30 Nov 2026.

judiciary: Independent courts headed by the Supreme Court and the Supreme Administrative Court; the Council on Legislation reviews draft bills.

elections.name: General election (Riksdag)
elections.note: Turnout 84.9%. Opposition parties won 176 seats against 173 for the Tidö parties. Seats and vote share: S 99 (28.0%), M 70 (19.9%), SD 62 (17.5%), V 30 (8.4%), C 25 (7.0%), KD 22 (6.2%), MP 22 (6.1%), L 19 (5.3%). Kristersson asked to be relieved of office on 17 Sep and now leads a caretaker government.

elections.name: General election (Riksdag)
elections.note: Regular election, held on the second Sunday of September. A snap election would be called if four PM votes fail; two have failed (15 Oct and 3 Nov 2026) and the third is set for 30 Nov 2026.

synopsis: The opposition parties (Social Democrats, Left, Centre and Greens) narrowly won the September 2026 election with 176 of 349 seats. They disagree over which parties should sit in government: on 15 October 2026 the Riksdag rejected Magdalena Andersson as prime minister of a Social Democrat-only government, and on 3 November it rejected the Centre Party leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist. Ulf Kristersson leads a caretaker government, and on 24 November the Speaker proposed him as prime minister of a Moderate, Centre, Christian Democrat and Liberal government; the Riksdag votes on 30 November, while the Centre Party is divided over a government that would depend on the Sweden Democrats.
policies: Caretaker government limited to routine business pending a new government
Measures against gang crime (outgoing government's agenda)
NATO integration and higher defence spending
challenges: Government formation deadlock: two failed PM votes so far, and a snap election follows if four fail
Disputes among the opposition parties over whether the Centre or Left Party should be in government
reviewNote: Confirmed: election results, seat counts, Kristersson's caretaker status and the PM votes of 15 Oct (248–99 against Andersson) and 3 Nov (324–25 against Thand Ringqvist, only the Centre Party voting yes) (Riksdag, 3 Nov). On 3 Nov the Speaker gave Ulf Kristersson the task of exploring whether a government the Riksdag will tolerate can be formed; on 17 Nov he gave an interim report and was given a further week, and on 24 Nov he gave his final report and the Speaker proposed him as PM of an M, C, KD and L government (Riksdag, 3, 17 and 24 Nov). The third PM vote is set for 30 Nov 2026 at 1 p.m.; a candidate is rejected only if more than half of all 349 members vote no. This is a nomination only: the Centre Party had taken no decision as of 25 Nov and faces internal opposition (The Local, 25 Nov). Executive, governing parties and Riksdag control stay as they are until the vote. Check the 30 Nov result before the next update.

name: Norway

legislature.name: Storting (169)
legislature.control: Labour minority, relying on centre-left parties
legislature.detail: Progress Party is the largest opposition party.

elections.name: Parliamentary election
elections.note: Labour re-elected; Progress Party surged to second.

synopsis: Støre's Labour Party governs alone in minority, with Jens Stoltenberg as finance minister. The sovereign wealth fund, energy and security dominate.
policies: Ethical guidelines for the sovereign wealth fund

name: Finland
judiciary: Supreme Court and Supreme Administrative Court.
synopsis: Orpo's centre-right coalition is pursuing austerity and labour-market reform, while President Stubb leads foreign and security policy as a NATO frontline state.
policies: NATO integration and border security with Russia

name: Iceland

elections.name: Referendum on resuming EU accession talks
elections.note: Rejected: No 118,047 (52.84%), Yes 105,338 (47.16%) of 223,385 valid votes; 897 blank and 749 invalid; turnout 82.6% (225,031 of 272,591 registered). Final count of the National Electoral Commission (Landskjörstjórn), announced on 2026-09-22.

synopsis: A coalition led by women party leaders is focused on stabilising the economy; voters narrowly rejected resuming EU accession talks in a referendum on 29 August 2026, and the Prime Minister has said the question is off the agenda for the rest of her term.
policies: EU accession talks shelved after the 2026 referendum
reviewNote: Referendum figures are the final count in the National Electoral Commission's report signed on 22 Sep 2026; Euronews and ABC (30 Aug 2026) report the same No win. The vote was advisory, but the government pledged to abide by it, and it said parliament, not the cabinet, would decide whether to formally withdraw the membership application (Euronews). No withdrawal had been reported in the sources read on 25 Nov 2026.

name: Estonia
synopsis: Michal's two-party government is very unpopular amid tax rises to fund defence, with Isamaa leading polls ahead of the March 2027 election.

name: Latvia

legislature.name: Saeima (100)
legislature.control: United List–National Alliance coalition majority (51 of 100)
legislature.detail: 15th Saeima (elected 3 Oct 2026): United List 41, Latvia First 17, Sovereign Power/Alliance of Young Latvians 15, National Alliance 10, Progressives 10, New Unity 7. Speaker: Edvards Smiltēns (United List), elected 3 Nov 2026.

elections.name: Saeima election
elections.note: Andris Kulbergs' United List won 41 of 100 seats; six lists entered the Saeima.

synopsis: Andris Kulbergs (United List) has led Latvia's government since 28 May 2026, after Evika Siliņa resigned. His centre-right United List won the 3 October 2026 election with 41 of 100 seats, and on 17 November the Saeima approved his second government, the 44th Cabinet of Ministers, by 57 votes to 34. It is a two-party coalition of the United List and the National Alliance, with 51 seats, and four of its ministries are led by non-party ministers.
challenges: A one-seat majority in the Saeima (51 of 100)

name: Lithuania
synopsis: Social Democrat leader Mindaugas Sinkevičius heads the third Social Democrat-led government of this Seimas term, sworn in on 14 July 2026. Inga Ruginienė's government resigned in June after the Social Democrats ended their coalition with Dawn of Nemunas and brought in the Democrats "For Lithuania".
